Why proof works better than checking a box

By the Quota team · Updated 6 October 2026

Short answer: A checkbox or a "done" message costs nothing to send, so it means very little, and it's easy to send one you didn't earn. Proof taken that day, like a photo or a short clip, takes a few seconds of real effort and is seen by people you know. That small cost is what makes skipping noticeable, and what makes the habit stick.

The problem with "done"

When a group checks in by text, the messages slowly shrink: "did 100", then "done", then a thumbs-up, then nothing. Each step is a little easier to fake, and once the group suspects people are faking, everyone stops trying.

What proof changes

  • It costs a little. Filming ten seconds of your last set takes effort, and that effort is a signal.
  • It is hard to fake. Especially if it has to be taken that day, rather than picked from an old camera roll.
  • It is interesting to see. Friends actually look at each other's clips, react and comment. A tick in a list gets no reaction.
  • It settles arguments. When proof is visible, "did they really?" turns into a quick look rather than a debate.

What good proof looks like

GoalGood proof
Pushups, squats, planksA clip of the last few reps or the final seconds
A run or walkA photo of the watch or app summary, or a clip outside
ReadingA photo of the page number you reached
Practising an instrumentA clip of you playing
StudyingA photo of the notes you made today
Cold showerA clip of the water running cold (keep it decent)

When proof is disputed

Sometimes a post clearly doesn't show the goal. The fairest fix is to let the group decide, not one person. A quick vote keeps it about the post, not about who called it out.

How Quota handles it. Quota only accepts a photo or a clip of up to ten seconds taken with its own camera that day, so nothing old from your camera roll gets through. Anyone can flag a post that doesn't show the goal, and the group votes on it.

Questions

Why is photo or video proof better than a checkmark?

A checkmark costs nothing and is easy to fake. Proof taken the same day takes a little effort and is seen by people you know, which makes skipping visible.

What counts as proof for a habit?

Anything that shows the goal was done today: a short clip of the last reps, a photo of a run summary, the page number you reached, notes you made.

What if someone posts fake proof?

Let the group vote on it rather than one person deciding. In Quota, anyone can flag a post and the group decides whether it counts.

Keep your goal with friends.

Quota is a free app for a daily goal with your group: proof before midnight, and a streak you keep together.
